title: 2020年12月四级真题 第2套 阅读2
paperTitle: 2020年12月大学英语四级真题（第2套）
passage:
P1 Forests in countries like Brazil and the Congo get a lot of attention from environmentalists, and it is easy to see why. South America and sub-Saharan Africa are experiencing deforestation on an enormous scale: every year almost 5 million hectares are lost. But forests are also changing in rich Western countries. They are growing larger, both in the sense that they occupy more land and that the trees in them are bigger. What is going on?

P2 Forests are spreading in almost all Western countries, with the fastest growth in places that historically had rather few trees. In 1990 28% of Spain was forested; now the proportion is 37%. In both Greece and Italy, the growth was from 26% to 32% over the same period. Forests are gradually taking more land in America and Australia. Perhaps most astonishing is the trend in Ireland. Roughly 1% of that country was forested when it became independent in 1922. Now forests cover 11% of the land, and the government wants to push the proportion to 18% by the 2040s.

P3 Two things are fertilising this growth. The first is the abandonment of farmland, especially in high, dry places where nothing grows terribly well. When farmers give up trying to earn a living from farming or herding, trees simply move in. The second is government policy and subsidy. Throughout history, governments have protected and promoted forests for diverse reasons, ranging from the need for wooden warships to a desire to promote suburban house-building. Nowadays forests are increasingly welcome because they suck in carbon pollution from the air. The justifications change, the desire for more trees remains constant.

P4 The greening of the West does not delight everyone. Farmers complain that land is being taken out of use by generously subsidised tree plantations. Parts of Spain and Portugal suffer from terrible forest fires. Others simply dislike the appearance of forests planted in neat rows. They will have to get used to the trees, however. The growth of Western forests seems almost as unstoppable as deforestation elsewhere.

questions.q: What is catching environmentalists' attention nowadays?
options: Rich countries are stripping poor ones of their resources.
Forests are fast shrinking in many developing countries.
Forests are eating away the fertile farmland worldwide.
Rich countries are doing little to address deforestation.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is catching environmentalists' attention nowadays? 是直接的特殊疑问句，问的 是一个具体事实，不含 infer、suggest、imply，也不问全篇主旨。

【拆句】题干 What is catching environmentalists' attention nowadays? 是现在进行时的特殊疑 问句，主语是疑问代词 What，谓语 is catching 带宾语 environmentalists' attention，时 间状语 nowadays 在句末。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。 51. What is catching environmentalists' attention nowadays? A) Rich countries are stripping poor ones of their resources. B) Forests are fast shrinking in many developing countries. C) Forests are eating away the fertile farmland worldwide. D) Rich countries are doing little to address deforestation.

【定位】Forests in countries like Brazil and the Congo get a lot of attention from environmentalists, and it is easy to see why. South America and sub-Saharan Africa are experiencing deforestation on an enormous scale: every year almost 5 million hectares are lost. 巴西、刚果这些国家的森林正得到环保人士的大量关注，原因不难看出。南美和撒哈拉以南 非洲正以巨大规模经历森林砍伐：每年几乎损失 500 万公顷。

【选项】A) 无中生有 原文只指出环保人士关注发展中地区的森林消失，并没说 Rich countries are stripping poor ones of their resources，这是套用国际关系常见话术编造出的内容。 B) ✓ 正确 Brazil and the Congo ↔many developing countries experiencing deforestation on an enormous scale ↔fast shrinking 预判说「发展中地区森林大规模消失」，Forests are fast shrinking in many developing countries. 在主语、动词、地域限定三处都与原文等值，是定位句的同义 替换。 C) 与原文相反 原文讲的是森林正在消失，选项却说 Forests are eating away the fertile farmland worldwide——森林在侵蚀农田，主客体关系恰好颠倒；首段也未提及 worldwide farmland 被吞噬。 D) 答非所问 题干问的是 What is catching environmentalists' attention nowadays?——环保人士 关注的是什么，而 Rich countries are doing little to address deforestation 是对富国 不作为的指责，原文首段并没有这一指控。 哪些国家的森林增长最快? A) 那些新近获得独立的国家。 B) 那些对木材需求最大的国家。 C) 那些过去森林覆盖率最低的国家。 D) 那些提供巨额政府补贴的国家。

questions.q: Which countries have the fastest forest growth?
options: Those that have newly achieved independence.
Those that have the greatest demand for timber.
Those that used to have the lowest forest coverage.
Those that provide enormous government subsidies.
questions.explain:
【判型】Which countries have the fastest forest growth? 直接问「哪些国家」，是对原文具体信 息的客观提取。

【拆句】题干 Which countries have the fastest forest growth? 是 Which 引导的特殊疑问句， Which countries 作主语，have 作谓语，宾语 the fastest forest growth。结构简单。 52. Which countries have the fastest forest growth? A) Those that have newly achieved independence. B) Those that have the greatest demand for timber. C) Those that used to have the lowest forest coverage. D) Those that provide enormous government subsidies.

【定位】Forests are spreading in almost all Western countries, with the fastest growth in places that historically had rather few trees. 几乎所有西方国家的森林都在扩展，其中增长最快的地方是那些历史上树木相当稀少的 国家。

【选项】A) 以偏概全 原文只用 Ireland 作为戏剧性案例（1922 年独立时 1%、现在 11%），并未说「森林增 长最快的是新近独立的国家」这一普遍规律，Those that have newly achieved independence. 是把单一举例拔高为通则。 B) 无中生有 the greatest demand for timber 在 P2 全段从未出现，森林增长最快的原因被原文限 定为「历史上树少」，而非木材需求。 C) ✓ 正确 historically had rather few trees ↔used to have the lowest forest coverage 预判说「历史上树木很少的国家」，Those that used to have the lowest forest coverage. 把「过去树少」换说成「过去森林覆盖率最低」，二者完全同义，因此 锁定。 D) 张冠李戴 enormous government subsidies 对应的是 P3 提到的 government policy and subsidy，那讨论的是「促进森林增长的因素」，不是 Q52 所问的「哪国增长最快」， 跨段错位。 历史上是什么促进了森林增长? A) 政府的倡导。 B) 木材用作燃料。 C) 有利的气候。 D) 环保运动。

questions.q: What has encouraged forest growth historically?
options: The government's advocacy.
The use of wood for fuel.
The favourable climate.
The green movement.
questions.explain:
【判型】What has encouraged forest growth historically? 问的是历史上具体促进森林增长的因 素，是对文中事实的提取，不要求多步推理。

【拆句】题干 What has encouraged forest growth historically? 是现在完成时特殊疑问句，What 作主语，has encouraged 作谓语，forest growth 作宾语，historically 是时间状语。现在 完成时强调「从过去延续到现在」的累积效应。

【定位】Throughout history, governments have protected and promoted forests for diverse reasons, ranging from the need for wooden warships to a desire to promote suburban house-building. 纵观历史，政府出于各种理由保护并推动森林的扩张，从制造木质战舰的需要，到希望促进 郊区住宅建设。 53. What has encouraged forest growth historically? A) The government's advocacy. B) The use of wood for fuel. C) The favourable climate. D) The green movement.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 governments have protected and promoted forests ↔The government's advocacy 预判说「历史上是政府保护并推动了森林」，The government's advocacy. 用名词形式 精准对应原文动词短语 promoted。 B) 偷换概念 原文虽提到 the need for wooden warships，但 warships 是用木材造战舰，并非烧木 头做燃料；The use of wood for fuel 偷换了用途。 C) 无中生有 原文讲历史上促进森林的是政府政策，没有提到 favourable climate 这一自然因素；这 是套用常识编造。 D) 张冠李戴 The green movement 属于近现代环保运动，对应原文 Nowadays 这一时间段，而题 干限定的是 historically 历史范围，时段不匹配。 是什么导致我们对森林的渴望日益增加? A) 它们独特的景观之美。 B) 它们作为果园的用途。 C) 它们改善空气质量的能力。 D) 它们稳定的建筑材料供应。

questions.q: What accounts for our increasing desire for forests?
options: Their unique scenic beauty.
Their use as fruit plantations.
Their capability of improving air quality.
Their stable supply of building materials.
questions.explain:
【判型】What accounts for our increasing desire for forests? 用 account for 直接问原因，对应 文中应有明确的因果句，属于事实信息提取。

【拆句】题干 What accounts for our increasing desire for forests? 中 account for 是固定短语， 意为「解释、是…的原因」。基础薄弱考生易把它误读成「算作」，须当心；除此之外句式 简单。

【定位】Nowadays forests are increasingly welcome because they suck in carbon pollution from the air. 如今森林越来越受欢迎，因为它们能吸走空气中的碳污染。 54. What accounts for our increasing desire for forests? A) Their unique scenic beauty. B) Their use as fruit plantations. C) Their capability of improving air quality. D) Their stable supply of building materials.

【选项】A) 无中生有 unique scenic beauty 在 P3 中并不存在；末段反而说 Others simply dislike the appearance of forests planted in neat rows，强调有人对景观不满，把「景观美」作 为渴求理由完全是无中生有。 B) 无中生有 use as fruit plantations 在 P3 全段未出现，原文用 plantations 是泛指「种植园」， 与水果无关。 C) ✓ 正确 suck in carbon pollution from the air ↔capability of improving air quality 预判说「森林能净化空气」，Their capability of improving air quality. 是这一句的标 准学术化转述，因此锁定。 D) 张冠李戴 supply of building materials 对应原文 wooden warships 与 suburban house- building，但那都是 Throughout history 段提及的历史理由，不是 Q54 所问的「如今 越发渴求」的理由。 作者对造林前景得出了什么结论? A) 撒哈拉以南非洲的沙漠将逐渐减少。 B) 它将在人们生活中发挥越来越重要的作用。 C) 发展中国家的森林破坏将迅速放缓。 D) 发达国家和发展中国家正朝着相反的方向发展。

questions.q: What does the author conclude about the prospects of forestation?
options: Deserts in sub-Saharan Africa will diminish gradually.
It will play a more and more important role in people's lives.
Forest destruction in the developing world will quickly slow down.
Developed and developing countries are moving in opposite directions.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author conclude about the prospects of forestation? 问的是作者对整 体前景的结论，覆盖全文走向，不可由单一定位句直接拿到。

【拆句】题干 What does the author conclude about the prospects of forestation? 是宾语从句 结构的特殊疑问句，What 是 conclude 的宾语，about the prospects of forestation 是 conclude 的状语，限定结论的话题对象。 55. What does the author conclude about the prospects of forestation? A) Deserts in sub-Saharan Africa will diminish gradually. B) It will play a more and more important role in people's lives. C) Forest destruction in the developing world will quickly slow down. D) Developed and developing countries are moving in opposite directions.

【选项】A) 偷换概念 Deserts in sub-Saharan Africa will diminish gradually. 蹭了 sub-Saharan Africa 这 一地名，但话题对象从「森林」被偷换为「沙漠」，原文从未讨论沙漠消长。 B) 过度推断 It will play a more and more important role in people's lives. 是抒情式价值判断， 与原文末句「两条趋势同样不可阻挡」的冷静对照不匹配；原文从未把森林作用提升到 「在人们生活中越发重要」的层面。 C) 与原文相反 原文末句明说 The growth of Western forests seems almost as unstoppable as deforestation elsewhere——他处毁林同样不可阻挡，而 Forest destruction in the developing world will quickly slow down. 却说「很快放缓」，方向相反。 D) ✓ 正确 The growth of Western forests seems almost as unstoppable as deforestation elsewhere ↔ moving in opposite directions But forests are also changing in rich Western countries. They are growing larger ↔Developed South America and sub-Saharan Africa ↔developing Developed and developing countries are moving in opposite directions. 同时容纳 了全文「造林与毁林」两条主线，与末句并置结构完美对齐，是唯一覆盖全文且不与任 何区间冲突的选项。
